title: New fire chief and Waterloo Park accessibility grant
subtitle: Development charge relief for a manufacturer, wildfire donation, library board appointments, and two early-stage rezoning applications.
overview: Council confirmed Sandy van Solm as Waterloo's new Fire Chief {{vote:m11}}, with a by-law enacting the appointment passed later in the meeting. The outgoing chief was thanked for service on retirement. Council also approved the City's application to the Build Communities Strong Fund for Waterloo Park accessibility upgrades, committing up to $830,000 of City money {{vote:m9}}.

To support a local manufacturer's expansion, council exempted the City portion of development charges, $42,720, for 650 Weber Street North, paid from the Economic Development Reserve {{vote:m12}}. Staff said the Region has confirmed it can exempt its portion too. Council donated $15,000 to the Canadian Red Cross wildfire fund {{vote:m13}}, and approved a new recruitment process for Waterloo Public Library Board citizen appointments {{vote:m10}}.

Council also approved the 2025 audited financial statements, revised Committee of Adjustment rules, a bakery lease at the Waterloo City Centre, and a demolition exemption at 36 Westhill Drive. Two informal public meetings on rezoning applications, at 153 Union Street East and 14 Roosevelt Avenue, drew questions and concerns. No decisions were made on either, and staff will report back later. A closed session also took place earlier in the day.

decisions.detail: Council approved the staff report and directed that a by-law be brought forward to appoint Sandy van Solm as Fire Chief.
Council approved the City's Build Communities Strong Fund application for Waterloo Park accessibility upgrades and committed up to $830,000 from three City funding sources.

decisions.item: Development charge relief, 650 Weber Street North
decisions.detail: Council exempted the City's non-residential development charge of $42,720 for the expansion, to be funded from the Economic Development Reserve when the building permit is issued.
Council donated $15,000 from its Community Priority and Contingency Reserve to the Canadian Red Cross wildfire fund.
Council approved a revised recruitment process for citizen appointments beginning with the 2027–2030 term, with the Clerk running it and the Board advising on applications.
Council approved revised terms of reference for the Committee of Adjustment and Fence Variance, and a new procedural by-law for the Committee.
Council exempted the property from the Demolition Control Area By-law so the dwelling can be demolished before site plan approval.
Council approved a lease with Roux Bakehouse at the Waterloo City Centre and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign it.

debate: On the development charge exemption, staff explained that the expansion would have qualified for the statutory industrial exemption if it had been physically attached to the existing building. Site constraints prevented that, so staff brought the case forward for council to decide. The business owner described those constraints, local co-op and apprenticeship hiring, and support for local tech companies.

At the 153 Union Street East informal meeting, councillors asked about traffic data collected while the nearby school was closed, rail whistle noise, emergency protocols for a rail line carrying hazardous materials, and fuel delivery noise from neighbouring businesses. Staff agreed to follow up on these in a later report.

A resident speaking for the neighbourhood said the technical studies gave inconsistent unit and parking numbers. They also raised concerns about building height next to low-density homes, rail noise and vibration, drainage and groundwater, and the deferral of technical details until after zoning. They asked for these to be resolved first.

Another resident questioned why 324 parking spaces were proposed when none are required, and expected most vehicles to exit onto Roger Street, causing congestion and safety concerns near the trail crossing. Staff said provincial rules mean parking in a major transit station area is set by the applicant, and they had asked about reducing surface parking.

On 14 Roosevelt Avenue, a councillor asked staff to look at a plain front facade, limited room for trees and green space, space for a transformer and mailbox, and reduced visitor parking. Staff said they would work with the applicant on these, including the option of removing a block of four units.
